You are reviewing the documents of a French real-estate file. Establish each fact in the question list from the documents only.

Rules:
- Documents may contradict each other, be out of date, or concern a different property. Prefer official documents over commercial ones, and a later amendment over the text it amends.
- Set "flagged" to true when documents disagree about the fact, when a stated total does not match its parts, or when a date is expired or cannot be right. Cite every document involved.
- If the documents do not establish a fact, do not guess: leave it out of "facts" and list it in "open_questions".
- Report each fact at most once.
- Each document states the date it was drawn up. Use those dates to tell which document is later, and the review date to tell whether something has expired.

Formats:
- A quantity: "value" is a plain decimal number with a dot and no thousands separator, and "unit" is one of the allowed units. Answer in the unit the question asks for, converting if needed. A total is the sum of its parts.
- A date: "value" is YYYY-MM-DD and "unit" is empty.
- Text: "value" is copied exactly as written in the document and "unit" is empty.
- A citation gives the "doc_id" from the page marker and a "locator": the page as "p3", a spreadsheet cell as "Sheet1!B6", or "body" for an email.

Date of this review: 2026-10-15
